observations: Photo shows a PlayStation 4 DualShock-style controller on top of a PS4 console box/cover (text at bottom reads “EASY GAMES & GADGETS”).
No clear photo of the PS4 console body, model label, serial/region, or internal status.
No visible game discs, storage capacity, or evidence of the claimed firmware/hack.

claims.claim: Ps4 fat hacked with fc26 and 8 other games
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show the PS4 console/model label, firmware/version, or any evidence of hacking or installed games.

claims.claim: Neatly used, never opened or repaired
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show seals, warranty stickers, or the console internals/underside.
Photo 0 cannot show temperatures, fan behavior, or thermal history.
Photo 0 does not show port testing (HDMI, USB, power) or a running console.

claims.claim: Comes with the original pads and the UK receipt
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a controller but does not show “original pads” contents or any UK receipt.

risks.risk: The item may not be a PS4 FAT (could be a different PS4 model) or may not be the console at all—photo mainly shows a controller/box cover.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the PS4 console front/back plus the underside/model label (CUH code) and serial number.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the worst case: unknown PS4 model/possibly not the console shown, so value should be treated as lowest for a remote sale.

risks.risk: The claimed hack/firmware (fc26) and “8 other games” may be false or not usable (e.g., account/installation issues).
risks.proof: A video clip of the console booting to the home screen showing the firmware/version and the game list (or installed titles) clearly.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not verified: treat as a standard console with no confirmed usable game library.

risks.risk: Ports may not work (HDMI/USB/power), or the console may have faults not visible in a still photo.
risks.proof: A short video showing HDMI output on a TV and testing at least: both USB ports, controller pairing, and power-on/off.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working/untested ports until proven.

risks.risk: Overheating/thermal issues may exist (common with older PS4 FAT units) even if it looks clean.
risks.proof: A video showing the console running a game for 15–20 minutes with fan noise/temperature readout (if available) or at least no shutdowns.
risks.if_unproven: Price as overheating risk: treat as needing servicing/repaste potential.

risks.risk: “Original pads” and “UK receipt” may be missing or not original.
risks.proof: Photos of the included accessories (controller(s), cables) laid out and a clear photo of the receipt.
risks.if_unproven: Price as missing/uncertain accessories and no receipt.

proof_requests: Clear photos of the actual PS4 console (front, back, and underside/model label with CUH code + serial).
Video of the console powering on and showing the firmware/version screen (to verify the claimed fc26).
Video showing the game list/home screen with the claimed titles (including the “8 other games”).
Video testing ports: HDMI to TV + both USB ports + controller pairing.
Photos of all included items laid out (controllers/cables) and a clear photo of the UK receipt.
response.reason: From photo 0, the PS4 console identity and the claimed hack/game/port status are not verifiable. Without a clear console/model label and a running test, any price would be guesswork.
